details.publicNotes:
When the stars first appeared in the skies over the celestial realms, not all of them were content with remaining in place. Unable to ignore their wanderlust, the first starborns pulled themselves out of the tapestry of stars and began to explore. Ageless and seemingly incapable of maturing, starborns enjoy reality with a childlike wonder that many travelers would envy, as they seem never to grow tired of the unending cosmos.

A starborn is a being with terrifying gravitational might, which they use to prank others and entertain themselves. These lonely beings mean well, but they are completely oblivious to the nature of their own strength, a tendency that occasionally brings misfortune to their playmates. However, their greatest vulnerability is their overly trusting nature, which often leads them to be manipulated into helping their friend's wishes come true, for good or for ill. Because of this, malefactors who befriend a starborn gain a formidable pawn in service to their schemes, often one significantly more powerful than any of their other allies.

Powerful Playmates

Eternal children despite their cosmic power and vast intellects, starborn enjoy playing with other children and take care never to harm or displease them. The same can't be said for the annoying adults who ruin their best games. These inconvenient guardians might find themselves walled away in an invisible prison, banished to the ceiling to live out their lives with reversed gravity, or even permanently teleported to a faraway land.

You repel effects that would hinder a creature or slow its movement. While under this spell's effect, the target ignores effects that would give them a circumstance penalty to Speed. When they attempt to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.SkZAQRkLLkmBQNB9]{Escape} an effect that has them @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.eIcWbB5o3pP6OIMe]{Immobilized}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.kWc1fhmv9LBiTuei]{Grabbed}, or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.VcDeM8A5oI6VqhbM]{Restrained}, they automatically succeed unless the effect is magical and of a higher rank than the unfettered movement spell.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spell-effects.Item.CdAyAiMGESvgNQtz]{Spell Effect: Unfettered Movement}

The target can understand all words regardless of language and also speak the languages of other creatures. When in a mixed group of creatures, each time the target speaks, it can choose a creature and speak in a language that creature understands, even if the target doesn't know what language that is.

Heightened (7th) The duration is 8 hours.

You spin secrets from the fundaments of magic, shaping them into a power with nearly unlimited potential. You duplicate a spell of 9th rank or lower of the tradition from which you cast manifestation, or a spell of 7th rank or lower from any tradition. Though you can normally choose only spells that are common or to which you have access, the GM might allow broader options.

You tear a minuscule hole in the fabric of reality, opening up a pinpoint portal that connects to the outskirts of a black hole deep in the void between worlds. Creatures and unattended objects in the area take 14d6 bludgeoning damage and are drawn toward the portal at the center of the area based on the results of their Fortitude save. If the spell would pull a creature or an object with at least 5 Bulk into an occupied space, the target is instead relocated to the nearest unoccupied square to its destination.

Dead or destroyed creatures and destroyed objects are not protected from entering and passing through occupied spaces; if they enter the portal's space, they are pulled through into the black hole and annihilated, and this movement through the portal has the teleportation trait.

Critical Success The creature or object is unaffected.

Success The creature or object takes half damage and is pulled up to 5 feet toward the portal.

Failure The creature or object takes full damage and is pulled up to 20 feet toward the portal.

Critical Failure The creature or object takes double damage and is pulled into the portal's space.

Heightened (+1) The damage increases by 2d6.

Area 4 40-foot bursts

You reach into the skies and call down an array of falling stars that explode upon colliding with the ground. Choose for the falling stars to be airbursts (sonic), asteroids (fire), comets (cold), or plasma (electricity). The spell gains the trait of the falling star type you chose. The four stars' central 10-foot bursts can't overlap. Each falling star deals 6d10 bludgeoning damage to each creature in the @Template[burst|distance:10] at the center of its area of effect before exploding, dealing 14d6 energy damage of the type you chose to each creature in its @Template[burst|distance:40]. A creature in any of the areas attempts one basic Reflex save against the spell no matter how many overlapping explosions it's caught in and can take each type of damage only once.

Heightened (+1) The bludgeoning damage increases by 1d10, and the energy damage increases by 2d6.

You crush the target by causing it to collapse in on itself, dealing 75 damage. The first time each round you Sustain the spell, you must choose a new target to be subject to the same effect; the same creature can never be targeted more than once with a single casting of this spell. You also can't affect more than one creature per turn with implosion. You can't target a creature that's incorporeal, gaseous, or liquid, or otherwise lacking a solid form.

Heightened (+1) The damage increases by 10.

You shroud a creature from others' senses. The target becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.VRSef5y1LmL2Hkjf]{Undetected}, not just to sight but to all senses, allowing the target to count as @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.zJxUflt9np0q4yML]{Invisible} no matter what precise and imprecise senses an observer might have. It's still possible for a creature to find the target by Seeking, looking for disturbed dust, hearing gaps in the sound spectrum, or finding some other way to discover the presence of an otherwise-undetectable creature.

You channel vital energy to heal the living or damage the undead. If the target is a willing living creature, you restore 1d8 Hit Points. If the target is undead, you deal that amount of vitality damage to it, and it gets a basic Fortitude save. The number of actions you spend when Casting this Spell determines its targets, range, area, and other parameters.

1 The spell has a range of touch.

2 (concentrate) The spell has a range of 30 feet. If you're healing a living creature, increase the Hit Points restored by 8.

3 (concentrate) You disperse vital energy in a @Template[emanation|distance:30]. This targets all living and undead creatures in the burst.

Heightened (+1) The amount of healing or damage increases by 1d8, and the extra healing for the 2-action version increases by 8.

You concentrate ethereal energy and attack a creature's spirit, dealing 16d6 spirit damage with a basic Fortitude save.

Heightened (+1) The damage increases by 2d6.

You form an @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.zJxUflt9np0q4yML]{Invisible} wall of pure magical force up to 50 feet long and up to 20 feet high. The wall has no discernible thickness. You must create the wall in an unbroken open space so its edges don't pass through any creatures or objects, or the spell is lost. The wall has AC 10, Hardness 30, and 60 Hit Points, and it's immune to critical hits and precision damage. The wall blocks physical effects from passing through it, and because it's made of force, it blocks incorporeal and ethereal creatures as well. Teleportation effects can pass through the barrier, as can visual effects (since the wall is invisible). Wall of force is immune to counteracting effects of its level or lower, but the wall is automatically destroyed by a @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.r7ihOgKv19eJQnik]{Disintegrate} spell of any rank.

Heightened (+2) The Hit Points of the wall increase by 20.

You move the target up to 20 feet, potentially suspending it in midair. When you Sustain the Spell, you can do so again, or you can shift your telekinetic focus to a different eligible target within range, moving it instead.

You instantly transport yourself and any items you're wearing and holding from your current space to an unoccupied space within range you can see. If this would bring another creature with you—even if you're carrying it in an extradimensional container—the spell is lost.

Heightened (5th) The range increases to 1 mile. You don't need to be able to see your destination, as long as you have been there in the past and know its relative location and distance from you. You are then temporarily immune for 1 hour.

With a rush of telekinetic power, you move a foe or something they carry. You can attempt to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.Dt6B1slsBy8ipJu9]{Disarm}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.7blmbDrQFNfdT731]{Shove}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.lOE4yjUnETTdaf2T]{Reposition}, or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.ge56Lu1xXVFYUnLP]{Trip} the target using a spell attack roll instead of an Athletics check.

You create a spatial ripple inside of a creature's body, injuring it from within. The target takes 1d6 slashing damage, with a basic Fortitude save. On a critical failure, the target is also @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 1}.

Heightened (+1) The damage increases by 1d6.

You create an orb of light that sheds bright light in a 20-foot radius (and dim light for the next 20 feet) in a color you choose. If you create the light in the same space as a willing creature, you can attach the light to the creature, causing it to float near that creature as it moves. You can Sustain the spell to move the light up to 60 feet; you can attach or detach it from a creature as part of this movement.

You can Dismiss the spell. If you Cast the Spell while you already have four light spells active, you must choose one of the existing spells to end.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spell-effects.Item.cVVZXNbV0nElVOPZ]{Spell Effect: Light}

Heightened (4th) The orb sheds light in a 60-foot radius (and dim light for the next 60 feet).

You hurl a loose, unattended object that is within range and that has 1 Bulk or less at the target. Make a spell attack roll against the target. If you hit, you deal 2d6 bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing damage—as appropriate for the object you hurled. No specific traits or magic properties of the hurled item affect the attack or the damage.

Critical Success You deal double damage.

Success You deal full damage.

Heightened (+1) The damage increases by 1d6.

description.value: The starborn doesn't need to breathe, and it's also immune to the effects of pressure extremes from the environment, such as the effects of being deep undersea or in outer space.

Trigger A creature within 100 feet casts a spell or makes a Strike that targets the starborn

Effect The creature must attempt a @Check[will|dc:42] save. On a failure, the starborn determine the targets, destination, and other effects of the spell or Strike, as though they were the caster or attacker.

When a starborn dies, their body collapses into an event horizon. All creatures within 100 feet must succeed at a @Check[fortitude|dc:42] save or be pulled 10 feet toward the sphere (20 feet on a critical failure). A creature that makes contact with the event horizon takes @Damage[20d6[void]] damage; if this reduces them to 0 Hit Points, they are annihilated.

Due to their connection to gravitational magic and the space element, the starborn is under the effects of subjective gravity at all times, regardless of the true gravitational features of the plane they are on.

The starborn enforces gravity in a @Template[line|distance:40|width:40]{40-foot cube} within 100 feet. First, they attempt to counteract all effects within the area that allow creatures to fly, hover, or otherwise avoid falling (counteract modifier [[/r 1d20+39 #Counteract]]{+39}). Then, they choose one of the cube's sides and set it as the new direction of gravity. All creatures in the area must succeed at a @Check[reflex|dc:47] save or be knocked @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.j91X7x0XSomq8d60]{Prone} by the disorienting shift. Creatures that can't fly immediately fall in the new direction. If they collide with a solid surface, they take the typical bludgeoning damage from falling. The starborn can't use Enforce Gravity again for [[/gmr 1d4 #Recharge Enforce Gravity]]{1d4 rounds}.
